```{r}

library(dplyr)

# read data
data <- read.csv(
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/sara_data_VM.csv",
  na.strings = "-999"
)

#now i want to see if the SART is actually correlated to the CAARS and BIS scores

#-----------------------------
# SART vs CAARS/BIS
#-----------------------------

sart <- c(
  "meanrt",
  "stdrt",
  "err_com",
  "err_om",
  "imp_err3",
  "imp_err_total",
  "d_prime"
)

self_report <- c(
  "dsm_inatten",
  "bis_first",
  "bis_second"
)

sart_results <- data.frame()

for(s in sart){

  for(sr in self_report){

    temp <- data[, c(s, sr)]
    temp <- temp[complete.cases(temp), ]

    test <- cor.test(
      temp[[s]],
      temp[[sr]],
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )

    sart_results <- rbind(
      sart_results,
      data.frame(
        SART = s,
        Self_Report = sr,
        N = nrow(temp),
        Rho = round(unname(test$estimate), 3),
        P = test$p.value
      )
    )

  }

}

# BH correction
sart_results$P_BH <- p.adjust(sart_results$P, method = "BH")

# Significance stars
sart_results$Sig <- ifelse(sart_results$P_BH < .001, "***",
                    ifelse(sart_results$P_BH < .01, "**",
                    ifelse(sart_results$P_BH < .05, "*", "")))

# Sort by significance
sart_results <- sart_results[order(sart_results$P_BH), ]

View(sart_results)

write.csv(
  sart_results,
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/SART_vs_CAARS_BIS.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

```
